body.x: Windamp (CEO Seong-Woo Ha, www.windamp.com) unveiled the "AF1010," a bladeless fan made with the air amplifying technology at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The AF1010 has no blades exposed, making for a safer fan for consumers. Its "Valley Breeze Technology’ has been patent-approved to mimic the breezes in a valley and was developed after noting breezes between buildings being cooler and stronger than on flat grounds.

Through this Valley Breeze Technology, the air current strength has been raised 50~100% while the electricity consumption rate of 15W reduces energy usage by 50%. The company added that the fan’s direct wind strength has also greatly increased.

The product’s two motors face each other and rotate together towards multiple directions to amplify the breeze. The breeze strength can also be controlled from a gentle breeze to a strong gust in 8 different levels. The fan can swivel up to 120 degrees and comes with an 8 hour timer so it can be safely utilized while sleeping.

“Through our participation in CES 2015, we plan to increase our presence in the overseas market and begin sales of our products in the global market,” shared a spokesperson for Windamp. “In the future we plan to introduce ceiling fans, indoor temperature regulating data centers, and other products.”
Windamp most recently took part in the IFA 2014 Hong Kong Electronics and Components show and has steadily been demonstrating its cutting-edge products to the world.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
